scope: Complete audited import inventory for Sude.sude_first_theorem and Sude.sude_first_theorem_values (Lean-checked proof relative to Sude.FiniteWitness for positive odd n < 2000 and 15 verbatim published analytic hypotheses from Rosser-Schoenfeld 1962, Bennett-Martin-O'Bryant-Rechnitzer 2018, and Montgomery-Vaughan 1973). Also retains the unused legacy Sude.BMORFinitePiFour record for historical provenance.

source_normalization.prime_enumeration: p_j is the j-th prime including p_1 = 2; j is a positive integer. Lean's primeOneBased j := Nat.nth Nat.Prime (j - 1) satisfies primeOneBased 1 = 2 and primeOneBased 2 = 3.
source_normalization.odd_prime_pool: oddPrime i := Nat.nth Nat.Prime (i + 1), starting at oddPrime 0 = 3; pool n := Set.range (fun i : Fin (n*n) => oddPrime i.val) contains the first n^2 odd primes.
source_normalization.prime_count_real: primeCountReal x := (((Finset.range (Nat.floor x + 1)).filter Nat.Prime).card : ℝ) counts primes p <= x on x >= 0, matching pi(x) in RS62 equation (1.1), p. 65.
source_normalization.pool_maximum: X = poolMaximum n := Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n*n) = p_(n^2+1) for n > 0
source_normalization.theta_ap: thetaAP x q a := sum over p in Finset.range (Nat.floor x + 1) of (if Nat.Prime p and (p : ℤ) % q = a % q then Real.log p else 0), matching theta(x;q,a) in BMOR (1.5), p. 429 and theta(x) = thetaAP x 1 0 in RS62 (1.2), p. 65 on x >= 1.
source_normalization.chebyshev_psi_ap: chebyshevPsiAP x q a := sum over n in Finset.Icc 1 (Nat.floor x) of (if (n : ℤ) % q = a % q then ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n else 0), matching psi(x;q,a) in BMOR (1.6), p. 430; proved equal to psiAP x q a for x >= 2 in Sude.chebyshevPsiAP_eq_psiAP.
source_normalization.bmor_critical_zeros: bmorIsCriticalZero χ ρ := 0 < ρ.re ∧ ρ.re < 1 ∧ DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ ρ = 0 (excluding Re ρ = 0 so imprimitive Euler factors never vanish, matching Z(χ) in BMOR Section 2.1, p. 438); bmorZeroMult χ ρ uses analyticOrderNatAt inside 0 < Re ρ < 1; bmorZeroCount χ T sums bmorZeroMult over |Im ρ| <= T (matching N(T,χ) in BMOR Definition 2.2, p. 440); bmorSatisfiesGRH χ H asserts Re ρ = 1/2 for all critical zeros with |Im ρ| <= H.
source_normalization.bmor_explicit_formula_terms: bmorSmoothFactor r τ = τ^(-r) * sum_{j=0}^r C(r,j)*(1 + j*τ)^(r+1) matches A_m(δ) in BMOR (2.4), p. 439; bmorU, bmorV, bmorW match U_{q,m}(x;δ,H), V_{q,m}(x;δ,H), W_q(x) in BMOR (2.5)-(2.7), p. 439 (with 67/5 = 13.4); bmorC1 = 399/1000 = 0.399, bmorC2 = 5338/1000 = 5.338 (Definition 2.4, p. 441); bmorVerifiedHeight d = 30610046000 for d=1 and 10^8/d for 1<d<=100000 (Definition 2.6, p. 441); bmorZeroFreeR = 28/5 = 5.6 (Proposition 4.34, pp. 478-479).
source_normalization.mv_pi: pi(x+y;k,a) - pi(x;k,a) for x > 0, y > 0 is counted exactly by (apInterval x (x+y) k (a : ℤ)).card, which filters primes p with x < p <= x+y and p = a (mod k).
source_normalization.bmor_pi_four: Legacy hypothesis Sude.BMORFinitePiFour in Sude/BMORFinitePiFour.lean:36 (NOT used by Sude.sude_first_theorem, Sude.sude_first_theorem_values, or Sude.tail_hasSquare; the file is imported only for the definitions liFromTwo and oddPrimeCountReal).

project_lemmas.scope: Explicit cyclic construction for J>=3 and 2J+1<=n, arbitrary main/anti choices; all row and column slots distinct, each four-cell rectangle has the required diagonal exclusions, center avoidance and disjoint supports. No prime supplies or controller conclusions.
Connects constructed disjoint coordinates to two physical diagonal trades, conditional on actual equal-gap values already occupying those coordinates.
Extends any injective assignment of actual pool values at distinct cells while preserving reserved cells, conditional on cell and value disjointness; does not prove balanced completion.
Composes placement, reservation preservation and two trades, conditional on a supplied injective family of equal-gap pool values; no prime-pair existence or controller conclusion.
All even subset sums through 2^(P+1)-2 for the distinct labelled binary gaps; does not establish any prime pairs.
A fresh even gap no larger than R+2 extends an existing complete even grid through R+gap. Physical bridge pairs and finite numerical gates remain open.
Any subset of already supplied, distinct-column physical row pairs is switched while tracking all row effects and preserving columns, diagonals, reservations and unselected entries.
Binary grid is realized by actual swaps under explicit physical pair and gap hypotheses. Prime-pair existence, placement and controller routing remain open.

Connects any proved complete subset-sum grid, including an extended bridge grid, to actual row swaps under explicit physical pair and reservation hypotheses; does not establish bridge pairs or finite numerical gates.
Proves disjoint endpoints for arbitrary actual primes above three with a common power-of-two gap, using the modulo-three obstruction; no finite population counts are proved.
A supplied positive-gap matching has exactly two distinct endpoints per pair.
Each previously reserved value eliminates at most one pair in a supplied matching; cross-stage population generation remains open.
Selects an exact requested number of matching pairs after charging earlier reservations, conditional on a sufficient candidate count.
Installs a supplied positive-gap matching in supplied distinct cells of an exact pool permutation, preserving earlier reservations; actual pool membership and cell geometry are explicit hypotheses.
For B>=2, proves every odd prime through B belongs to the first n² odd primes when the exact odd-prime count through B is <=n²; the five reported numerical counts are not yet certified.

Composes a conditional odd-prefix bound, actual candidate primality, fixed-gap matching, reservation depletion and exact Q selection into 2Q distinct actual-pool entries; no large finite count is assumed as an import.
Soundness of recursively checked Lucas node factorization and modular gcd conditions, starting without assumed primes; acceptance of the full table is not established.

Kernel checks 2418 recursive Lucas nodes and row arithmetic for the first 250 odd orders. Pool identities remain open; see first425_cover for the larger checked interval.

Constructs the repeated q/P/R labelled prime target list, proves oddness, actual-pool real radius, both axis-total identities and the prime diagonal target, conditional on identifying the row X and T with the actual pool. Individual diagonal corrections and the pool-prefix computation remain open.

Kernel checks 3918 recursive Lucas nodes and row primality, oddness, compatibility, radius, mean and integer-domain arithmetic for all first 425 odd orders. Pool maximum and total identities and remaining 8317 rows are open.
Constructs an off-diagonal derangement layer, disjoint from reservations, with exactly two distinct cells per row and column, under explicit load and size bounds; no prime supplies.
Installs explicitly supplied distinct pool entries and pair gaps into a balanced physical layer, preserving earlier reserved cells and entries.
Packs two successive balanced layers without cell reuse; see pack_and_install_two_networks for arbitrary finite row and column sequences under explicit supplied-value hypotheses.

Arbitrary finite row layers of supplied derangements, with pairwise-disjoint actual cells, exact aggregate row/column counts, all supplied distinct pool values and gap equations, and preservation of initial reservations; supply and load premises explicit.

Transposes the construction to original coordinates and avoids both diagonals for network cells. Transposition itself preserves the labelled diagonal sums; installation preserves initial reserved entries but may rearrange unreserved diagonal entries.

Composes row and column layer networks with separate globally injective and mutually disjoint pool-value families, retaining all actual placements and gaps and exact combined per-line counts; no supplies or flow theorem are assumed as imports.
Proves the integer PB8--PB9 capacity substitution given the exact count of d*S layers; numerical premises remain open.

Performs arbitrary selected installed row and column swaps with exact signed line effects, preserving columns during row switches, rows during column switches, both diagonals, prior reservations and pool; does not construct the selected sets.

Derives the exact public square only from an actual installed placement, prime targets and diagonals, and actual selected subsets satisfying every displayed transfer; selection and controller remain open.
Proves signed even subset sums relative to the lower even midpoint and its exact rounding bound, assuming an actual complete even grid.
Constructs a fixed physical reference orientation with all stated even signed transfers available through actual swaps; this handles one supplied reservoir, not a multi-edge flow.
Finite disjoint reservoirs have one fixed reference and simultaneously chosen subsets for any supplied bounded even transfers, assuming each complete grid and pairwise block disjointness.

Realizes supplied even row and column edge transfers simultaneously by actual disjoint pair swaps from one reference, with exact line effects and reservation/diagonal/pool preservation; no flow existence.

Realizes any supplied integral flows bounded by floor(N/2) when each explicit reservoir grid has coverage >=2N; all line corrections are twice directed divergences. Does not establish the needed flows, reservoirs or midpoint identity.
Proves the precise integer floor inequality for the 999/1000, 199/200 and KX>=2000 FC2K rounding gate; does not establish a controller or cut inequality.

From an installed physical network and complete disjoint even grids, selects one reference first and derives HasSquare n for any supplied bounded integer flows satisfying all prime-target divergence equations, assuming the starting diagonals prime. Any supplied bounded integer flow has zero total divergence and satisfies all cut bounds under the exact signed edgeTransfer convention used by the physical switches. This is the necessary direction only, not max-flow/min-cut sufficiency.
